anomalies.observed: The AVR-ISP-6 header J4 has pin 1 (MISO) connected to PWM, pin 3 (SCK) connected to SCK, and pin 5 (RST) connected to RST, but pin 4 (MOSI) has no wire or net label. The ATtiny MOSI/PB0 pin is on the SDA net at U2.5/U3.5, but that net is not connected to J4.4.
anomalies.expected: For an in-system programming header labeled AVR-ISP-6, pin 4 (MOSI) should be connected to the MCU MOSI/PB0 net (here SDA) so the ATtiny can be programmed through the header.

evidence.quote: J4 AVR-ISP-6: pin 1 MISO -> PWM, pin 3 SCK -> SCK, pin 5 RST -> RST; pin 4 MOSI is unconnected

anomalies.impact: In-system programming via J4 is not possible; a blank MCU could not be programmed through the intended ISP header, preventing the board from functioning as designed after assembly.

parsed.summary: The schematic appears mostly coherent, but the AVR-ISP-6 header is missing the MOSI connection, which would prevent programming the ATtiny through the intended interface.
